about: H3: story text and narration per piece, built by tools/narration.py from questions.json (the curator) and records.json (MoMu). Derived file: edit the sources, then rerun the script.
voices: per piece in `voice`: gemini:<model>:<voice> or picsart:<voice>

ST503.title: Jak
paragraphs:
Blue taffeta, fine and smooth,
with a soft shine.
Along the warp, white and yellow
threads float free:
a zigzag that breaks into flowers.

Square at the neck,
close to the elbow,
long skirts falling from the waist.
Metal hooks and eyes
hold the open front,
and inside, unseen, blue linen
striped white and yellow.

ST80930.title: Ikat vest
paragraphs:
Dark blue cotton in double ikat,
light blue spots
and small red squares.

Long sleeves, puffed full.
The front panels cross
over each other
and close at the waist with ribbons.

A waistcoat, or a jacket?
The record calls it both.

ST2434.title: Green wool coat
paragraphs:
Green broadcloth,
falling into tails.
Two rows of four buttonholes,
and no buttons left to close them.

Eight round brass buttons
wait apart, loose,
once, most likely,
sewn on at the back.
Two flat ones stay,
signed M and Cie, Paris.
Later, someone added
a broad band of red,
and inside, a lining
of glossy purple.

ST80931.title: Monpe trousers
paragraphs:
Dark blue cotton in ikat,
light blue spots,
small red squares:
monpe, trousers that puff.

A broad waistband,
and long ribbons to close it.
At the ankles, ribbons too,
to tie them close,
if you wish.

ST2062.title: Knee breeches
paragraphs:
Cream woollen broadcloth,
every stitch by hand.
Six buttons close the long fly,
a small pocket hides
in the waistband at the right hip,
a brass buckle draws in the back.

At each knee, a slit
and three buttons.
Inside, a glimpse
of glossy cream twill,
probably silk.
Once, part of
a Russian military costume.

ST81114AB.title: Blouse
paragraphs: This white cotton blouse has machine-made lace on the front, the collar, and the ends of the sleeves (named the cuffs). Take a look at the centre front of the blouse, the lace pieces frame a panel of pleats (the columns of fabric folded double and sewed). If you look closely you can see this pleated panel is attached to the rest of the blouse with buttons. These shiny white buttons are made of mother of pearl, the strong and smooth inner layer of certain sea shells, such as oysters. The buttonholes are hand sewn

The blouse is part of an outfit that would have been worn by women for cycling around 1900. The type of fabric used for the blouse, called ‘cotton batiste’ is very light and breathable, making it a good fit for cycling and exercising.

ST81116.title: Trousers
paragraphs: Take a look at these black woollen trousers. They are wide and gather at the knees with an elastic, forming a kind of balloon shape. Both in the front and the back are six deep pleats or folds which hide the part where the left and right pant legs are attached.

If you take a few steps back, you may find it is hard to see whether these are trousers or a skirt. The voluminous trousers are part of an outfit worn by women around 1900 for cycling. Around this time, many women started wearing trousers to cycle as long skirts could get caught in the wheels. In contrast to their daily clothing, newly designed sports clothes gave women more comfort and room to move when exercising.

ST2407/1-2.title: Football boots, Dirk Bikkembergs
paragraphs:
White leather,
wound with blue circles,
made for a football club:
FC Bikkembergs Fossombrone,
in the Marche, Italy.

Look under the studs:
the clear sole shows
a drawing in red and blue.
A leather circle covers the laces,
held on with elastic.
One heel blue, one heel red,
the club's badge on the left,
the label's on the right.

ST80881.title: Furisode kimono
paragraphs:
Ecru silk, painted,
touched with gold.
Broad ribbons billow across it
in many colours,
and behind them a landscape drifts:
houses, clouds,
peonies and chrysanthemums,
plum blossom,
Japanese maple, bamboo.

Look closer at the flowers:
their details are embroidered
in silk and metal thread.

ST655/1.title: Cocktail dress
paragraphs:
Green and black,
in horizontal stripes,
eleven covered buttons
down the front.
A shawl collar of black velvet,
short sleeves edged in velvet too.

And a secret in the cut:
the skirt is made of half circles,
with no side seams,
so the stripes run across the front
and turn upright at the back.
Inside, a black ribbon holds the hem,
fixed by hand in fine stitches.

ST2435.title: Sequin silk dress
paragraphs:
Ecru silk, calf-length,
covered all over in sequins
that shimmer like pearls.

A wide boat neck.
Straight panels, falling.
The sides stay open,
caught by three hooks and eyes
on the left,
and short strips at the hips
that draw the line in.
Over it all, machine stitching
in metal thread
traces curls and eyes.

ST652/1.title: Polka-dot mended dress
paragraphs:
Blue cotton, scattered
with small white and red dots,
buttoned all the way down.
Mended, and mended again,
in patches of checked cloth.

Red edges the pockets
and the sleeves,
three red lines trim the right lapel,
and from the chest pocket
a red handkerchief
seems to peek out.
A cloth belt ties at the front
to mark the waist.

ST673/1-2.title: Cotton combinaison
paragraphs:
White cotton,
and no boning at all:
a bodice and long drawers,
buttoned into one.
Broderie anglaise frames
the V of the neck,
ruffles circle the arms,
mother-of-pearl buttons
close the front.

Bone buttons ring the waist
to hold what was worn on top.
It was made for sport:
tennis, croquet,
badminton, archery.

ST81190.title: A.F. Vandevorst Jacket
paragraphs: This grey woolen jacket from 1998-1999 by Belgian fashion house A.F. Vandevorst has some remarkable details. It is made up of separate parts; the sleeve, front, shoulder, and breast pieces are not sewn together. If you look closely, how are they held together? The pieces, as well as the darts and side seams are fastened with metal rivets, bolt-like fasteners that attach two fabrics. The jacket is closed in the centre front by a column of snap buttons, a type of button you can easily close by pressing the two ends together.

Now look at the back of the piece. What stands out? The red cross stitched at the nape of the neck is the iconic logo of A.F. Vandevorst. Since their early collections, their designs have been inspired by German artist Joseph Beuys, religion, horses and their tack, uniforms, rivets, lingerie, and fetish shoes. This jacket is part of their first collection.

ST80998.title: Striped velvet bridal kaftan
paragraphs:
A bride's kaftan,
in velvet striped
burgundy, red, green and black.
The neckline rounds,
then falls to a point,
and the long sleeves taper
to points of their own.

Over the chest, along the sides,
across the sleeves,
cords and metal thread
are sewn on in many colours,
on grounds of orange,
light brown and green.
Under the sleeves' embroidery,
a lining of pink cotton.

ST2431/1-4.title: Light-blue cavalry uniform
paragraphs:
A lieutenant's uniform,
light blue and red,
for the National Guard,
the mounted chasseurs of France,
the ninth regiment
or the eighteenth.

Black braid crosses the chest
and becomes the fastening.
A red collar stands up,
worked in coiled metal thread.
Red trousers carry a blue stripe,
and a kepi,
fifteen centimetres tall,
wears a black leather peak.

ST2432/1-2.title: Dark-blue tailcoat uniform
paragraphs:
A coat for the National Guard.
Dark blue broadcloth,
a high red collar,
red cuffs, tails lined in red,
their points turned out
so the red shows below the blue.
Three white-metal buttons
still say Garde Nationale.

The trousers came later,
and a red lace was set
into their back later still.
Coat and trousers,
both altered with time.

ST671.title: Silk walking dress
paragraphs:
Beige silk rep,
a long gown for walking.
On the waistband, a printed name:
Madame Guédon Deschamps,
83 Boulevard Magenta, Paris.

Machine lace at the throat,
in imitation of Lille bobbin lace,
its standing collar
held up with bones.
Beneath, a second dress of silk,
its pleats showing under the hem.
At both sides,
the hem hangs a little lower.

ST2203.title: Black satin dress
paragraphs:
Black silk satin,
close to the body.
A deep V, edged in black velvet,
broad shoulders
padded with white cotton.

Down the front and the back,
the satin gathers and drapes.
Two draped pockets
sit at the hips,
five fabric buttons
close each cuff,
and from the point of the V
a black metal zip
runs twenty centimetres,
to the waist.
